it names the Muninn `github` tool
call to use instead
stumbles.why: Muninn is never explained, and it's unclear what the `github` tool is or how it avoids the 403. A reader outside the project can't tell what to use.
The text doesn't say why a session gets 403, such as missing token scope or a sandbox restriction. That makes it hard to judge whether the guard is the right fix.

point: The guard that blocks GitHub release and tag creation from a session, because those calls return 403, now also catches `gh api` POSTs to `/releases` and `/git/refs`, and 4 new tests cover the change.
